intent: Make the issue dashboard (~/src/issue-dashboard) one click away from the i3 bar: an [issue_dashboard] block shows issues to do, agents working and work ready to merge, turns red when an agent or a proof failed, and a click opens the dashboard window the same way [book_guard] opens book-guard.
scope: Non-goal: the dashboard itself (lives in ~/src/issue-dashboard, local repo); i3/i3blocks were not reloaded on the live session.
changes: issue_dashboard.sh reads the one-line status.json the dashboard server rewrites on every refresh (~/data/issue-dashboard/status.json): '📋 <to do> · ⚙ <working> · ✓ <ready>', white normally, green when something is ready to merge, red with '· ✗ <n>' when an agent or a proof failed, grey '📋 dashboard' when the file is missing, unreadable or older than 180 s (server not running). Zero forks on the hot path: one builtin read, bash regex, printf clock.
A click runs ~/.local/bin/issue-dashboard-desktop via setsid -f, which reuses the dashboard server or starts it detached and opens an app window.
~/.config/i3blocks/issue_dashboard.sh symlinked to the repo file, the way i3/install.sh links every i3blocks/* file.

verification.evidence: fresh / ready / failed / stale / missing / broken / empty / click asserted; strace shows exactly one execve (bash) and no clone/fork on the hot path.
All i3blocks efficiency regression tests passed.

'📋 5 · ⚙ 0 · ✓ 0' #FFFFFF while the server ran against Sepci0/kado-no-akari; '📋 dashboard' #6272A4 before it had ever run; BLOCK_BUTTON=1 started the launcher, which opened the (stubbed) browser with --app=http://127.0.0.1:8765/.

risks: The block appears only after the next i3 reload; nothing was reloaded on the live session.
A click with issue-dashboard-desktop missing does nothing (errors are silenced so the bar never breaks).
rollback: git revert this commit and remove ~/.config/i3blocks/issue_dashboard.sh; i3-msg reload.
Confirm the bar still renders [book_guard] and the other blocks.
